title: Carbon Isotope Discrimination - Part I - Trapline
author: Stephen Driever
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qywdxxe

steps.title: Clamp leaf and reach steady state
steps.instruction: Clamp the leaf in the LI‑6800 cuvette under bright ambient light, adjust the H₂O reference (H2OR) so leaf temperature (Tleaf) is ~25 °C (maintain within ±0.03 °C), avoid mechanical tension, illuminate from above with ≥200 µE, let the plant acclimate in the lab for ~24 h, then wait until assimilation (A), fluorescence and stomatal conductance (gs) are stable for a 10‑min window (≈2 h total, checking every ~15 min after the first 30 min).

steps.title: Set LI‑6800 environmental parameters
steps.instruction: Manually match the LI‑6800, set automatch OFF and Fluorescence OFF, control temperature on the block (Txchg) not on the leaf, keep Tleaf within ±0.03 °C of 25 °C (the C₃ calculation reference), and adjust humidity or Txchg as needed.

steps.title: Switch inlet gas to low O₂
steps.instruction: When steady state is reached, switch the inlet gas to 2 % O₂ using the flow controller set to ~6, change the constant value in the LI‑6800 accordingly, note that assimilation will change and may oscillate before stabilising, and verify that with no flow the O₂ reading is ≤0.5. Keep a backup O₂ cylinder ready.

steps.title: Activate and cool cold finger
steps.instruction: Turn ON the cold finger (ON/OFF only), place it in the acetone dewar, cover the dewar top with foil, avoid resting the finger on the dewar bottom, and wait until the acetone turns milky white and its temperature is below –70 °C (≈1 h).

steps.title: Prepare LN₂ dewars and vacuum lines
steps.instruction: Fill two dewars three‑quarters full with liquid nitrogen for trap immersion and two additional dewars three‑quarters full with LN₂ for gas condensation; open the glass valves on each preparation line and adjust pump valves (providing support from below and applying downward pressure while twisting) until the vacuum gauge reads ≈5.5 mbar on each line (≈1 h), then verify that both collection tubes are open.

steps.title: Verify leaf stability before collection
steps.instruction: Re‑check that the leaf remains in a stable state (both A and gs unchanged) before proceeding.

steps.title: Immerse traps in liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Immerse both gas‑collection traps (distillation tubes) in liquid nitrogen (using the two LN₂ dewars), ensuring the tubes are covered close to the top.

steps.title: Seal vacuum and ready collection tubes
steps.instruction: Close the glass valves, twisting perpendicular to flow direction, and watch the vacuum drop to low 10⁻² or high 10⁻³ mbar; for each preparation line, confirm the collection tube is open.

steps.title: Condense acetone and remove dewars
steps.instruction: When the vacuum stabilises (all gas re‑condensed), remove the acetone and liquid‑nitrogen dewars, collect any acetone drips from the distillation tube into a beaker, close the tube, and take it out of LN₂.

steps.title: Replace collection tube and purge line
steps.instruction: Remove the used collection tube from the preparation line, let it thaw on a rack, insert a new empty open collection tube, and open the pump valve to purge the line and remove residual air.

steps.title: Record fluorescence baseline
steps.instruction: Take a fluorescence measurement (Fm′/Fs) and set the LI‑6800 timer to log data every minute for 5 min (autoprogram).

steps.title: Sublimate trapped CO₂ in cold acetone
steps.instruction: In one motion, remove the distillation tube from LN₂ and submerge it in cold acetone to sublimate the frozen CO₂; the pressure in the preparation line should rise as gas is released.

steps.title: Seal collection tube and recondenser
steps.instruction: Close the collection tube, then quickly submerge it in liquid nitrogen (covering at least the bottom 2 cm) to recondense the released gas; the pressure should fall again as gas is drawn into the tube.

steps.title: Shut low‑O₂ cylinder
steps.instruction: Close the low‑O₂ cylinder and adjust the constant value in the LI‑6800 accordingly.
